title: Trump's New Arc de Trump Renderings Looked Like Vanity With Federal Stationery
description_short: Trump's New Arc de Trump Renderings Looked Like Vanity With Federal Stationery
description_medium: The Trump administration released renderings for a proposed 250-foot triumphal arch at Memorial Circle, near Arlington Memorial Bridge, the Guardian and Washington Post reported. The design included a 60-foot golden Lady Liberty and was intended to mark the nation’s 250th anniversary. Officials had begun seeking formal approval, while military veterans sued, arguing the structure would alter views of Arlington National Cemetery.
description_long:
On April 10, 2026, the Trump administration released renderings of a proposed 250-foot triumphal arch at Memorial Circle, near the Arlington Memorial Bridge. Harrison Design’s plan included a 60-foot gold-colored Lady Liberty figure and was presented as a monument for the country’s 250th anniversary. The Washington Post reported that officials had begun seeking formal approval for the project.

The proposal faced a lawsuit from military veterans, who argued that the structure would alter views of Arlington National Cemetery and the surrounding memorial landscape. The released drawings made the scale and location of the project public, but did not constitute final approval or guarantee construction. The Guardian and Washington Post described a plan entering review while its effect on a prominent civic setting was being challenged. No settled construction schedule or final design was reported. The immediate dispute concerned whether a large new monument should be built at Memorial Circle and how it would change the views and setting of nearby national memorials.

title: Trump Promised Peace, but Dearborn Got Another Reminder of the Lie
description_short: Trump Promised Peace, but Dearborn Got Another Reminder of the Lie
description_medium: Associated Press reporters found Dearborn families waiting for news from relatives in Lebanon and mourning those already lost as the Iran conflict widened. Wayne County official Assad Turfe said he feared for an uncle and his family. The report set those anxieties against Trump’s promise of Middle East peace and the city’s large Arab American community.
description_long:
The Associated Press reported from Dearborn, Michigan, as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran widened to Lebanon. Residents with family ties across the region waited for updates and mourned relatives killed in the conflict. Wayne County official Assad Turfe told AP that he was worried about an uncle, his wife, their children and grandchildren in Lebanon. Dearborn has one of the largest Arab American communities in the United States, and the article described how the conflict was discussed in mosques, at vigils and around family tables.

AP placed those fears alongside Trump’s earlier promise to bring peace to the Middle East. The report also noted that the community did not hold one political view: Turfe had been among the few Arab Americans to endorse Kamala Harris in 2024. Its account was a local portrait of the conflict’s human consequences, seen through residents’ uncertainty about loved ones abroad. It did not claim that Dearborn residents responded uniformly or that the promise alone explained their views.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Promised Peace, but Dearborn Got Another Reminder of the Lie

title: Trump: Baron Trump is born
description_medium: Baron Trump is born. The first child of Donald and Melania Trump, Baron, is born. This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, legal development, documented relationship, or policy consequence linked directly or indirectly to Trump. The downstream effects include institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long:
CBS/AP reported that Donald and Melania Trump’s son was born on March 20, 2006. The baby was Donald Trump’s fifth child and Melania’s first. Donald announced the birth in a telephone interview on MSNBC about 20 minutes after the baby arrived, saying that everyone was well. The report said Melania had been in labor for eight hours. CNN’s Larry King later reported the name Barron William Trump.

Donald and Melania had married in Palm Beach in January 2005. Donald’s three older children, Donald Jr., Ivanka and Eric, were from his marriage to Ivana Trump; his daughter Tiffany was from his marriage to Marla Maples. The contemporary report noted the family background as it covered the birth and the television interviews that carried the announcement. Regis Philbin, a friend of Trump, called him on air after hearing the news and Trump told him, “She gave me a nice son.” The article identifies the newborn, records the announcement and places it within the family’s public life at the time.

title: Trump: Jared & Ivanka vacation in Croatia with Wendi Deng, meet with Russian oligarch
description_short: Trump: Jared & Ivanka vacation in Croatia with Wendi Deng, meet with Russian oligarch
description_medium: In August 2016, Ivanka Trump posted a photograph with Wendi Deng while vacationing in Croatia with Jared Kushner. TrumpFile says Mueller investigation records later described a meeting during the trip with an unnamed Russian oligarch and his girlfriend. The page does not identify them or describe what was discussed.
description_long:
Ivanka Trump posted a photograph with Wendi Deng from Croatia on August 14, 2016, while she and Jared Kushner were on vacation there. The TrumpFile timeline later reported that records from Robert Mueller’s investigation disclosed that a Russian oligarch and his girlfriend had also joined the trip. The timeline said the oligarch’s name had not been released publicly.

The account placed the trip during the 2016 presidential campaign, when Kushner was involved in Trump’s campaign. It did not describe a conversation among the travelers, any political discussion, or an exchange of information. The photograph documents Ivanka Trump and Deng together; the later account of the unnamed guests comes from investigative records described in the timeline. The guest’s identity and the purpose of the meeting remain undisclosed, so the reported contact alone does not establish an agreement or wrongdoing. The surrounding story has also attracted speculation about Deng’s relationships, but those claims are separate from the reported presence of the unnamed Russian guest.

title: Trump: The NRA spends $30 million to help elect Donald Trump through illegal coordination
description_short: Trump: The NRA spends $30 million to help elect Donald Trump through illegal coordination
description_medium: In 2016 the NRA and Trump’s campaign ran television ads on matching dates and networks, with the purchases handled by separate firms. The linked account says Jon Ferrell authorized both sets of buys and quotes former FEC general counsel Larry Noble calling the overlap strong evidence of coordination. It does not cite a ruling that found a violation.
description_long:
The linked account says the National Rifle Association spent about $30 million supporting Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign. On October 19, 2016, the NRA purchased television ads through Red Eagle Media, while the campaign separately bought ads on the same networks for matching dates and times through American Media & Advocacy Group. Jon Ferrell, a chief financial officer at the company that placed the buys, authorized both sets of purchases, according to the report.

Former Federal Election Commission general counsel Larry Noble described the overlap as “very strong evidence, if not proof,” of illegal coordination. His statement was an expert assessment, not a legal determination. The linked report does not cite an FEC ruling or court finding that the NRA and campaign violated campaign-finance law. The parallel purchases and shared authorization prompted questions about whether the spending was coordinated, but the documented record supports describing the ad buys and the concern they raised rather than calling a violation conclusively established.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: The NRA spends $30 million to help elect Donald Trump through illegal coordination
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: The NRA spends $30 million to help elect Donald Trump through illegal coordination

title: Trump purges 46 attorneys from the DOJ, including one asked to investigate him
description_short: Trump purges 46 attorneys from the DOJ, including one asked to investigate him
description_medium: Attorney General Jeff Sessions requested the resignations of 46 U.S. attorneys appointed under Obama in March 2017. The TrumpFile account says ethics watchdogs had urged New York U.S. Attorney Preet Bharara to investigate possible Emoluments Clause violations, but it does not say a formal investigation had begun or link his departure to that matter. Officials said the mass resignations had been planned earlier.
description_long:
In March 2017, Attorney General Jeff Sessions asked 46 U.S. attorneys appointed under President Barack Obama to resign. Preet Bharara, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York, was among those asked to leave. The mass request came after the administration had initially asked U.S. attorneys to remain in place, making the scope and timing of the resignations a subject of public attention.

The linked account notes that watchdogs had urged Bharara to investigate whether Trump’s business dealings raised Emoluments Clause concerns. It does not report that a formal investigation had begun or establish that Bharara’s departure was ordered to stop one. Sean Hannity had called for a purge of Obama-era officials the day before the resignation requests, while administration officials said the plan had been made earlier. These events occurred close together, but the source does not establish that one caused the other. The documented action was a broad turnover of federal prosecutors, including Bharara, amid separate calls for scrutiny of Trump’s business interests.

preserved_fields.title: Trump purges 46 attorneys from the DOJ, including one asked to investigate him
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump purges 46 attorneys from the DOJ, including one asked to investigate him

title: Trump: Rep. Dana Rohrabacher meets with Julian Assange for a pardon quid pro quo
description_short: Trump: Rep. Dana Rohrabacher meets with Julian Assange for a pardon quid pro quo
description_medium: Representative Dana Rohrabacher met Julian Assange, activist Charles Johnson and Assange’s lawyer at the Ecuadorian Embassy in London in 2017. The linked account says Assange wanted an assurance against arrest in exchange for information about Russia’s role in the 2016 leaks, and Rohrabacher said he would raise an arrangement with the White House. It does not show Trump approved a pardon.
description_long:
Representative Dana Rohrabacher met Julian Assange, activist Charles Johnson and Assange’s lawyer at the Ecuadorian Embassy in London in August 2017. The linked account says Assange offered information that could support the claim that Russia was not responsible for the 2016 WikiLeaks disclosures, while seeking assurance that he would not be arrested if he left the embassy.

Rohrabacher later said he believed someone had extracted the emails and attributed the hack to Russia, and that he hoped the meeting could help establish that. He told the account he would return to the White House and see whether an arrangement could be made. The reporting describes a proposed exchange and a request for protection, not a pardon granted or an agreement authorized by Trump. It does not report that the White House accepted the proposal or that Assange’s information was verified. The meeting and Rohrabacher’s stated intention to raise the matter are documented; the alleged deal should not be treated as completed.

title: Trump: McConnell and Rand Paul block sanctions on Kremlin company and Manafort business partner
description_short: Trump: McConnell and Rand Paul block sanctions on Kremlin company and Manafort business partner
description_medium: The Senate voted 57–42 on a measure to restore sanctions on Rusal, falling short of the 60 votes needed to advance it. Mitch McConnell opposed the effort, and Rand Paul also voted against it, the linked account reported. Rusal was associated with Oleg Deripaska, a business associate of Paul Manafort; the vote did not itself establish why the senators opposed the measure.
description_long:
On January 16, 2019, the Senate voted 57–42 on a measure to restore sanctions against Rusal, a Russian aluminum company associated with Oleg Deripaska, a business associate of Paul Manafort. The resolution fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance. Eleven Republicans joined Democrats in supporting it; Mitch McConnell opposed the effort, and Rand Paul also voted against it.

The House had previously voted 362–53 to restore the sanctions. The linked account cited a later Senate Intelligence Committee report describing Rusal as a tool in Vladimir Putin’s influence efforts. The Senate vote was a procedural outcome: the sanctions measure did not advance. The connections among Rusal, Deripaska and Manafort provide context for the debate but do not establish why individual senators voted as they did. The account also distinguished the vote from later plans for investment in a Kentucky aluminum project. The event was the Senate’s failure to reach the threshold, not a decision that cleared Deripaska or Rusal of scrutiny.

title: Trump: Judge orders Donald Trump to pay $2m for illegal use of charity funds
description_short: Trump: Judge orders Donald Trump to pay $2m for illegal use of charity funds
description_medium: A New York judge approved a settlement requiring Trump to pay $2 million and make 19 admissions about use of Trump Foundation funds. The agreement covered money used for his businesses and campaign, including funds from an Iowa veterans’ fundraiser. The case was a state civil proceeding, not a criminal conviction.
description_long:
In November 2019, a New York judge approved a settlement in the state attorney general’s case over the Trump Foundation. Donald Trump agreed to pay $2 million and made 19 admissions about the charity’s use of money. He acknowledged that the foundation bought a $10,000 portrait of him that was displayed at a Florida hotel, paid obligations of for-profit businesses including Mar-a-Lago and a Westchester golf club, and gave his presidential campaign control of about $2.8 million raised at an Iowa veterans’ fundraiser.

The settlement addressed the foundation’s use of charitable funds for Trump’s businesses and campaign. The $2 million payment was below the $8 million the attorney general had sought. The agreement resolved the state proceeding on those terms and included Trump’s admissions; it was not a separate criminal conviction. The court-approved result provides a documented account of specific transactions and the remedy imposed. The Iowa fundraiser was presented as a campaign event, and the settlement required the remaining charitable assets to be distributed to eligible charities.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Judge orders Donald Trump to pay $2m for illegal use of charity funds
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Judge orders Donald Trump to pay $2m for illegal use of charity funds
